# Pawlak Information System

A **Pawlak information system** is the pair `S = (U, A)`: a universe `U` of objects, a set `A` of
attributes, and for each attribute `a ∈ A` a function `a: U → V_a` assigning every object a value.
It is the formal substrate of **rough set theory** — deliberately weaker than a relational schema,
because the point is what you can say when objects are only distinguishable through their attribute
values.

## Indiscernibility

For any attribute subset `B ⊆ A`, the **indiscernibility relation** `IND(B)` holds between two objects
when they agree on every attribute in `B`. It is an equivalence relation, so it partitions `U` into
equivalence classes — the finest distinctions `B` can make. Rough set theory builds lower and upper
approximations of a target set from those classes: what `B` *definitely* proves, versus what it
merely *permits*.

## As a property graph

Lab 6 of [[discrete-mathematics-laboratories]] models `S = (U, A)` as a **bipartite graph** rather
than a table:

```
(:Object)-[:HAS_VALUE {value}]->(:Attribute)
```

39 objects × 25 attributes = **975 `HAS_VALUE` edges**. Putting the value on the *relationship*
rather than on the object is the modelling move that makes it an information system rather than a
row: attributes become first-class, so "which objects agree on this attribute" is a one-hop traversal
instead of a column scan.

These counts are real. The Cypher was executed against a live Neo4j Desktop instance:
